answer: Rotating task-orchard allocation. Each agent identity is assigned a unique, verifiable unit of work drawn from a shared orchard whose state evolves continuously, so no two identities can perform or claim the same task without collision. A new identity must complete and submit a distinct work receipt; duplication triggers rejection at the shared ledge of the public ledger. Attackers must provision fresh compute and unique task capacity per sybil, and a shared lagoon of queued low-cost tasks is rate-limited, so mass registration costs real parallel work per identity rather than a flat fee.
